Note::TexAccessor::commands¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::commands() const
TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::commands(bool with_args) const

Extract Complete Control-Word Lexemes¶

commands() locates TeX control words in every Text cell. A control word is a backslash followed by ASCII letters or @; an immediately following * is part of the lexeme. The default form returns the command spelling itself, including its leading backslash: \section* remains \section*.

The Boolean overload controls argument capture, not filtering. With with_args == false, it is exactly the default operation. With with_args == true, scanning continues through every immediately attached, balanced optional group ([...]) and required group ({...}). ASCII spacing between the command and those groups is retained. Nested groups are balanced, so a title such as {A {nested} title} is one argument rather than a truncated match.

Argument capture is lexical. It deliberately does not know a command’s arity, expand macros, validate whether a command exists, or interpret argument meaning. It captures the consecutive groups that are present. If the next group is unbalanced, that group is not attached; the control word is still a valid result. Comments also remain visible to this scanner. Run strip_comments() first when commented-out commands must be excluded.

Control symbols are not control words. In particular, \\ is a linebreak and \$ is an escaped symbol; neither is reported. This prevents text following a linebreak from being misread as part of a command. Use command_names() when only names without the leading backslash are required, and args(name) when the payload of one known command is the actual result.

The result is a closed TokenBatch: tokens() is a flat Text Note in source order, while offsets() is an Int64 Note with one cumulative boundary per input cell plus the initial zero. Duplicate commands remain duplicated. Undefined input yields undefined tokens and offsets [0]; cells without commands contribute an empty range. Text is required. The receiver is not mutated, and extraction performs one lexical pass per cell plus storage for the returned lexemes and offsets.

Example 1: Default Command Lexemes¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\section* [Short] {A {nested} title} and \alpha)",
    R"(line break: \\beta; escaped: \$; malformed: \frac{one)",
    "plain text"});
const auto commands = source.tex().commands();

std::cout << commands.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\section*", "\\alpha", "\\frac"]

The linebreak and escaped dollar are control symbols, so neither contributes a token. The malformed fraction still contains the valid control word \frac.

Example 2: Include Balanced Arguments¶

const auto complete = source.tex().commands(true);
std::cout << complete.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\section* [Short] {A {nested} title}", "\\alpha", "\\frac"]

The optional and required groups attached to \section* are retained as one token. The incomplete {one group is not captured.

Example 3: Spell Out The Default¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << (source.tex().commands(false).tokens() == commands.tokens())
                 .all().bool_item()
          << '\n';

Output¶

true

Example 4: Offsets Preserve Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = complete.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Example 5: Undefined Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().commands();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";

Output¶

false offsets=[0]

Example 6: Non-Text Input Rejects¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().commands(true);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "commands Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

commands Int64: rejected

See Also¶
